reviews.comment: The class claims to teach philosophy, yet exams and quizzes are just memorization of every little detail of the films and readings. Lectures consist of the students just talking about their ideas about the films, nothing is really taught and there is no point in attending class besides taking the quizzes every week. Homework is several hours long.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Conway is great if you're genuinely interested in philosophy. Your entire grade is 2 tests and a project, so be aware that you need to do really well on those two exams if you want a good grade. He's a good teacher and clearly loves what he does. Attendance is not mandatory & if you study and read the material, you can get an A or B pretty easily.

Professor Conway steamrolled discussion and came off as pretentious and self-aggrandizing. He made digs at students about the ideas discussed likely being hard for them to understand and seemed to revel in being a "savior figure" to the class. Quizzes and exams were movie trivia that didn't speak to the philosophical themes of the material.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Beautiful lectures, driven by dialogue. Make sure to participate! Take good notes in class, and if you really understand the material, you'll do well. Write as much as you can on exams (I would fill up the entire big bluebook and received a 100+). You always get what you put into a course

Conway has no canvas. Not helpful. Not friendly. Not clear that he even understands the material. His lectures amount to pseudo-intellectual posturing and drivel. His grading system is laughable and shockingly incoherent, should be looked into by his department. There is literally no good reason to take this guy. His other reviews are 100% bots.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally one of the greatest professors I've ever had. He makes discussions very engaging and I never felt so conflicted with all the new ideas he introduced. Class was almost completely discussion with him occasionally doing some powerpoints, and the content from the powerpoints was also tested. The test are "glorified movie trivia."
Dr. Conway is an incredibly smart and fun professor. Take notes while watching the assigned movies/readings, it will help so much when it comes to quizzes and tests since they are mostly trivia!

Dr. Conway is an amazing man and absolutely is here to teach us what he knows. This class is graded by a few easy exams, and is entirely discussion based outside of that. He picks good movies that help further what is discussed. If you need the special credit, or just an elective, I highly stress taking this class.

If you can get Dr. Conway on your schedule, finalize that ASAP. Dr. Conway is an amazing prof who encourages learning and engagement, not information chugging. He will work with you so long as you communicate with him. He wants your feedback and will basically give test answers and questions. The class is also super fun!

I was so excited for this course as I'm extremely passionate about the subject matter, so I really wanted to love this class. However, there's always something kind of off with his lectures, they often feel passive-aggressive? When it comes to the lectures, it's all about the philosophy but quizzes and exams are glorified trivia tests, 75% names.

This class requires readings and watching a movie weekly. The tests were difficult and there was only 2. Participation was a major part of the grade. Professor Conway is a nice guy and he is interesting to listen to, but if you miss classes you will have a difficult time with the tests.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Conway is solidly one of my favorite professors at A&M. He chose interesting movies for us to discuss and discussions were essentially all we did for the semester! His in-class discussions were thought-provoking and I generally just enjoyed this class Warning though, your only grades are 2 mandatory and 1 optional test, study hard!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This guy is super nice until hes not. He will correct you in front of the class, and he makes it seem like your questions are dumb. The grading criteria for tests were hardly specified, and he takes major points off for grammar. Managed to squeeze out an A but he was not easy to work with. Very passive aggressive emails as well.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: **This went from in person to online due to COVID-19** Dr. Conway became one of my favorite profs when I took his Philosophy of Religion class. His lectures are pretty heavy so get ready to think, and he opens them up for discussion a lot. His tests are pretty hard- you write until you run out of class time. But I found he graded fairly on them.

His lectures are very interesting and he is funny. Your grade comes from one paper that he grades very harshly, but you can resubmit for a better grade as many times as you want. There are also three exams, and he takes your two best grades.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE HIM SO MUCH! we didn't have any tests. we wrote one short paper and watched films and read parts of a few books and then discussed in class. a truly caring prof, an easy A, and my favorite class in all aspects. i am hoping to take him again :)

Dr. Conway is a very liberal teacher, but his lectures are so interesting that it is fairly easy to look past that. Your grade is based on 2 tests which concerned me at first, but after I got a 100 on the first test (completely written) I wasn't worried. However, he does require a 15 min poem presentation if you want an A in the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Blatantly liberal but bearable. Focuses class time on discussion of the films and prefers for students to voice opinions. No real lecture style - interjects into students' discussions with key terms he will put on exam. 2 exams, optional cumulative final, participation (10%). Don't bother w/reading; just watch the films and write down terms/ideas.

Dr. Conway's class was tough, but manageable. Class consisted of 3 tests (1 is optional) and 1 paper, which he grades very critically. His class is lecture oriented and his lectures are very entertaining and very interesting. You're only required to read 6 books, but all you need are good lecture notes to ace the test. Overall great professor!

He is a great professor.  He is one of those professors that enjoys watching students learn for themselves as opposed to teaching.  He heavily encourages cross talk and discussion during the class, and though he does lecture he manages to make them enjoyable by purposefully playing devils advocate.  Also, there is only one essay all semester!

Professor Conway was super cool and extremely helpful. All I had to do was show up to class and listen to the discussion. The best thing is that we only had to write 1 essay all semester and you could turn it in as many times you wanted. Would definitely take any class he's teaching.

He was super cool. Show up to class and listen to discussion. His exams are very easy if you pay attention during class. Participating in discussion is not required, but encouraged. The class presentation is the hardest part of the course, but you can work in groups.
